Report_ID: Hematoma expansion (>6-mL absolute increase in hematoma volume)
Title: Tranexamic Acid for Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Trial (ISRCTN50867461)
Author: Nikola Sprigg et al.
Comment: For the planned intention-to-treat synthesis, randomized denominators (TA 16; placebo 8) were used. Table 4 reports follow-up 24-hour CT availability of 16 and 7, respectively, yet reports placebo hematoma expansion as 1 (12.5%), which uses the randomized placebo denominator of 8. No risk ratio was recorded because the paper's own Results section does not explicitly report one; it is left for downstream calculation from the extracted 2×2 counts. The paper reports enrollment between March 2011 and April 2012, so study_year was left null rather than selecting one year.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Tranexamic acid') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Single-center, prospective, phase IIa, randomized 2:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled, blinded-endpoint pilot trial
Study Environment: Nottingham University Hospital NHS Trust stroke service; single-center hospital trial
Content length: 1-g loading-dose infusion over 10 minutes followed by a 1-g infusion over 8 hours
Topic of Content: Antifibrinolytic treatment to limit hematoma expansion after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage
interaction_type: Randomized treatment administration with blinded endpoint assessment
Participant type: Adults with acute (<24 hours after ictus) spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage
Recruitment source: Stroke service at Nottingham University Hospital NHS Trust
Outcome measurement: Blinded CT volumetric analysis; hematoma expansion defined as greater than 6-mL absolute increase in hematoma volume from day 1 to day 2
Outcome variable: Hematoma expansion (>6-mL absolute increase in hematoma volume)

Report_ID: Dichotomous occurrence of any positive haematoma-volume growth by 24 hours
Title: Tranexamic Acid as Antifibrinolytic Agent in Non Traumatic Intracerebral Hemorrhages
Author: Ananda Arumugam et al.
Comment: The article does not define a conventional dichotomous expansion threshold (for example, ≥33% or ≥6 mL). The treatment count 11/15 is explicitly stated for any positive growth. The control count 15/15 is derived by tallying the 15 positive patient-level volume differences in Table 2; it is not stated as a single fraction in prose. Randomised denominators of 15 per arm were used as required by the synthesis plan. No RR was reported by the paper, so no risk ratio was entered. The limitations section reports withdrawals, but Tables 2 and 3 each contain 15 patients with repeat-scan data.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Tranexamic acid plus strict blood-pressure control') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Study Environment: Department of Neurosurgery, Hospital Sultanah Aminah Johor
Content length: 1 g IV bolus over 10 minutes followed by 1 g/hour infusion for 8 hours
Participant type: Adults with acute primary spontaneous non-traumatic supratentorial hypertensive intracerebral haemorrhage
Recruitment source: Patients admitted to Hospital Sultanah Aminah Johor
Outcome measurement: Any positive planigraphic haematoma-volume difference between baseline and 24-hour CT, based on the paper's use of ‘expansion’ for positive changes
Outcome variable: Dichotomous occurrence of any positive haematoma-volume growth by 24 hours

Report_ID: Participants with haematoma expansion at approximately 24 hours/day 2, defined as an absolute increase of more than 6 mL or relative growth greater than 33%
Title: Tranexamic acid for hyperacute primary IntraCerebral Haemorrhage (TICH-2): an international randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 superiority trial
Author: Sprigg et al.
Comment: The paper calculated the displayed expansion percentages among participants with repeat imaging (265/1054 and 304/1058). Per the synthesis contract, the extracted pooling denominators are the numbers randomised: 1161 tranexamic acid and 1164 placebo. Thus the ITT risks for synthesis are 265/1161 and 304/1164; the reported percentages should not be applied to the randomised denominators. Design Type: International multicentre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group phase 3 superiority trial

Country: Denmark, Georgia, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Malaysia, Poland, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey, and the UK
Participant type: Adults with acute spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage admitted within 8 h of symptom onset
Recruitment source: Acute stroke units at 124 hospital sites in 12 countries

Report_ID: Intracerebral haemorrhage growth (>33% relative growth or >6 mL absolute growth by 24 h [±3])
Title: Tranexamic acid in patients with intracerebral haemorrhage (STOP-AUST): a multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial
Author: Meretoja et al.
Comment: The reported odds ratio was adjusted for baseline intracerebral haemorrhage volume. One participant in the tranexamic acid group lacked a follow-up scan because of early palliation and was assigned the growth outcome under the prespecified analysis plan; intention-to-treat randomised denominators of 50 per arm were retained. The paper did not report a risk ratio; use the extracted arm-level events and totals for RR synthesis.
Design Type: Prospective, double-blind, multicentre, parallel-group, placebo-controlled phase 2 randomised trial
Participant type: Adults with acute non-traumatic, spot-sign-positive intracerebral haemorrhage
Recruitment source: 13 hospitals in Australia, Finland, and Taiwan
Outcome measurement: Presence of intracerebral haemorrhage growth on repeat CT by 24 h (±3), defined as >33% relative growth or >6 mL absolute growth from baseline
Outcome variable: Intracerebral haemorrhage growth (>33% relative growth or >6 mL absolute growth by 24 h [±3])
